case.case_title: Chandrasiri v. Gen. Cyril Ranatunga and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1993) 1 Sri L R

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner's detention and subsequent rehabilitation order violated Article 13(4) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that his detention and the order for rehabilitation were invalid and violated Article 13(4) as punishment can only be imposed by a competent court.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents argued that the detention and rehabilitation were lawful under Emergency Regulations and based on recommendations by police officers.
key_facts: Petitioner detained under Emergency Regulations and sent for six months rehabilitation at Aesthetic Centre, Madiwela.
O.I.C. Urubokka Police recommended release due to lack of charges against petitioner.
Rehabilitation order was based on a letter referring to 46 detainees but did not mention petitioner by name.
Detention was found invalid by the Court.
Rehabilitation order is valid only if detention is valid.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 13(4) as prohibiting punishment except by a competent court and that detention before trial is not punishment. The Court held that an order for rehabilitation is only valid if the detention itself is valid.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the Court found the petitioner's detention invalid, the order for rehabilitation based on that detention was also invalid and violated Article 13(4). The Court noted the rehabilitation order was not properly justified and was an assumption by the respondents.
principles_established: Detention before trial is not punishment but must be lawful.
Orders for rehabilitation depend on the validity of detention.
Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court.

outcome.holding: The Court held that the order for rehabilitation was invalid and violated Article 13(4).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation and costs awarded as part of relief for unlawful detention and invalid rehabilitation order.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(4) was central to the Court's reasoning on the invalidity of the rehabilitation order, linking the legality of detention to the permissibility of rehabilitation as a non-punitive measure.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court found the rehabilitation order invalid because it was based on an invalid detention and was not properly justified by the police letter which did not mention the petitioner by name.
